outcome: Two new dimensions were closed since the frozen revision: n≥17 (Pang, June 2026) and n=16 (Kafidov, July 2026, building on Pang), neither yet digested by a named human expert; a third preprint (Li, Xiong, Yang, ~Aug 2026) gives an alternative certificate for n=4, which was already proved before the window (Dec 2023) and so is not itself a new case. Dimensions 5–15 remain open; the conjecture as a whole is still open.

ai.basis_quote: The proof strategy, the joint-deficit scaling lemma, and most of the original proof text were produced by OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol through ChatGPT in response to prompts from Boris Kafidov. ... Boris Kafidov selected the problem, directed the interactions and revisions, and is the sole named author; he assumes responsibility for the final manuscript and for any submission of it. The AI system is acknowledged as a reasoning and writing tool, not as an author.

summary: The frozen January 2024 statement of the Dittert conjecture (uniquely maximized at A=(1/n)Jₙ) had, before the window, already been settled for n=2 (Sinkhorn, 1980s), n=3 (Hwang, 1987) and n=4 (Divya K.U. and Somasundaram, arXiv:2312.00464, submitted 1 Dec 2023 — this is open_stale territory for that case, not a change in this window). Within the window: Zhekai Pang (arXiv:2606.01531, submitted 1 Jun 2026, Universitat Pompeu Fabra) proved the conjecture for every n≥17, combining the Knopp–Sinkhorn bound with a refined Cheon–Wanless scaling argument; no AI involvement is disclosed anywhere in that paper. Boris Kafidov (arXiv:2607.19439, submitted 21 Jul 2026) then closed n=16, explicitly disclosing that 'the proof strategy, the joint-deficit scaling lemma, and most of the original proof text' were produced by OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol (released 9 Jul 2026, confirmed via independent search) via ChatGPT, with Kafidov directing the process and taking authorship responsibility — this is squarely ai_role=generated per §6.2 (the model produced the mathematics that is in the result: the strategy, the central lemma, and most of the text). Together, Pang + Kafidov reduce the open range to 5≤n≤15. A third preprint (Li, Xiong, Yang; arXiv:2607.29191, ~Aug 2026) gives an independent exact sum-of-squares certificate, MOSEK-discovered and Lean-verified, for n=4 — but n=4 was already resolved in Dec 2023, so this is a re-proof of an already-settled case, not new territory, and discloses no LLM use (only SDP solving and Lean formal verification, which are not AI systems under §6.2). None of the three 2026 preprints have been digested by a named human expert (no Tao blog post, no Quanta piece, no journal acceptance found); the only 'review' located is an automated AI-reviewer site (Pith Review), which flagged a citation gap in Kafidov's equality-case argument (an unverified reliance on Hwang's Proposition 2.1(ii)) and recommended conditional acceptance pending a fix — this is not expert digestion and does not qualify the paper for `resolved`. Wikipedia's live article was checked directly and has NOT been updated to reflect any of the 2026 results: its most recent substantive edit is from 12 January 2026 (an authorlink fix), predating all three preprints; the triage's claim that 'the conjecture's Wikipedia article now reflects the n≥17 result' is not borne out and is flagged as a disagreement. Given this, status is `partial` (cases n=16 and n≥17 newly settled within the window, general conjecture for 5≤n≤15 still open) and the decisive event for ai_role purposes is the Kafidov n=16 paper, since it is the one carrying AI involvement.
competing_reading: One could argue the decisive `event` should instead be Pang's n≥17 result, since it is the larger and more consequential piece of progress (settling all but finitely many dimensions) and carries no AI involvement, which would leave ai_role as `none` for the 'main' event and relegate Kafidov's GPT-generated n=16 result to a secondary note. I chose to foreground the Kafidov paper because this record must reflect the AI question centrally, and it is the specific event this problem contributes to the AI-involvement count; both are reported and dated in the record.
what_would_settle_it: A named human expert (e.g. a specialist in permanent/doubly-stochastic-matrix combinatorics, or a Tao-style blog digestion) reading and either endorsing or rejecting the Pang and Kafidov arguments, including resolving the citation gap flagged in the Kafidov paper; a full proof or disproof for the remaining range 5≤n≤15; and a check of whether Wikipedia's article is ever updated to reflect these preprints.
